category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statements: All auditors are analysts. Some analysts are planners. Conclusions: I. Some auditors are planners. II. All auditors are analysts.
solution: Conclusion II directly restates the first statement. Conclusion I does not necessarily follow because the analysts who are planners need not be auditors.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statements: No inspectors are clerks. Some clerks are accountants. Conclusions: I. Some accountants are not inspectors. II. No accountant is an inspector.
solution: The clerks who are accountants cannot be inspectors, so some accountants are not inspectors. Nothing establishes that every accountant is a clerk.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statements: All permits are documents. No document is confidential. Conclusions: I. No permit is confidential. II. Some documents are permits.
solution: Every permit is a document and no document is confidential, so no permit is confidential. Existence of permits is not stated.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statements: Some researchers are writers. All writers are readers. Conclusions: I. Some researchers are readers. II. All readers are writers.
solution: The researchers who are writers are necessarily readers. The reverse relationship is not given.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: The municipality introduced an online permit system, and the average processing time fell substantially within three months. Conclusions: I. The online system may have contributed to faster processing. II. Every municipality should immediately adopt the same system.
solution: The observed association supports a cautious possible inference, but it does not prove that every municipality should immediately adopt the same system.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: A survey found that employees who received regular feedback reported higher job satisfaction than those who did not. Conclusions: I. Regular feedback is the only cause of job satisfaction. II. Regular feedback is associated with higher reported satisfaction.
solution: The survey establishes an association, not a sole causal explanation.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: The library extended its opening hours during examination month after students requested longer access. Conclusions: I. Students value access to the library. II. All students requested the extension.
solution: The request and response support the first conclusion. The statement does not say all students made the request.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: A road was closed for maintenance for seven days, during which traffic was diverted to an alternative route. Conclusions: I. The original road required maintenance. II. The alternative route was shorter.
solution: The closure for maintenance directly supports I. No comparison of route lengths is given.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: The office should publish a plain-language guide to its new application procedure. Assumptions: I. Applicants may have difficulty understanding the current procedure. II. A clearer guide could help applicants follow the procedure.
options: Both I and II are implicit
solution: The recommendation presumes both a communication difficulty and that clearer guidance can address it.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: The department should add more public-service counters on peak days to reduce queues. Assumptions: I. Peak-day demand can create long queues. II. Additional counters can help handle the demand.
solution: Both assumptions are necessary for the recommendation to make sense.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: The school should provide a digital copy of the timetable to parents. Assumptions: I. Parents may need convenient access to the timetable. II. Every parent owns a smartphone.
solution: Convenient access is a reasonable implicit basis. Universal smartphone ownership is not required by the recommendation.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: The agency should train frontline staff before launching the new service. Assumptions: I. Staff knowledge can affect service delivery. II. Training can improve staff readiness.
solution: The proposal relies on both the relevance of staff competence and the usefulness of training.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Assertion (A): A department should keep a backup of important digital records. Reason (R): Digital records can become inaccessible because of hardware failure or other technical problems.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
solution: Technical failure is a direct reason why backup copies are needed.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Assertion (A): A committee should record the reasons for major decisions. Reason (R): Recorded reasons can improve transparency and allow later review.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both true, but R does not explain A
solution: The reason directly supports the practice of recording reasons.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A city experienced unusually heavy rainfall, followed by localized flooding in low-lying areas. Which is the most reasonable inference?
options: Heavy rainfall can be a contributing cause of localized flooding
Flooding always occurs whenever it rains
solution: Heavy rainfall can exceed drainage capacity and contribute to flooding; the other options make unjustified absolute claims.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A factory installed preventive maintenance software, after which unplanned machine downtime decreased. Which conclusion is most justified?
options: The software is proven to be the only cause
The decrease may be related to improved maintenance planning
solution: The timing suggests a possible contribution, but it does not establish exclusive causation.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A public office receives repeated complaints that citizens cannot easily find its service requirements online. Courses of action: I. Redesign the information page using clear headings and a checklist. II. Stop publishing service requirements online.
solution: Improving clarity addresses the complaint; removing information would worsen access.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A school notices a sudden increase in absenteeism. Courses of action: I. Examine attendance records and consult students and families. II. Punish every absent student immediately without investigation.
solution: Fact-finding is appropriate before deciding on interventions. Blanket punishment without understanding causes is not.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A water-supply office finds that one neighborhood has repeated leakage complaints. Courses of action: I. Inspect the relevant network and identify the source. II. Replace every pipe in the entire city immediately.
solution: Targeted inspection is proportionate. Citywide replacement without diagnosis is excessive.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: An examination board discovers that a published notice contains an incorrect application deadline. Courses of action: I. Issue a corrected notice promptly through the same official channels. II. Leave the error uncorrected to avoid confusion.
solution: Prompt correction reduces harm and ensures applicants receive accurate information.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Five reports P, Q, R, S and T are arranged from first to last. P is before R. Q is after S. T is before P. Which report can be first?
solution: T must be before P, and P before R; Q must be after S. Therefore T can be first.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Six tasks A, B, C, D, E and F are scheduled in six slots. A is immediately before B. C is before D. E is after B. Which pair must occupy consecutive slots?
solution: The condition explicitly makes A immediately before B.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Four officers K, L, M and N have different ranks. K is senior to L. M is junior to N but senior to L. Who must be the most senior?
solution: N is above M, and M is above L. K is above L but is not compared with N; therefore the statement set does not force N to be above K. Thus no option is necessarily most senior.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Seven files are processed in an order. File H is third. File J is immediately after K. File L is before K. Which file cannot be first?
solution: H is fixed in the third position, so it cannot be first.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Five people A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. B sits immediately to the right of A. C sits at the left end. E sits to the left of D. Which arrangement is possible?
solution: In C-A-B-E-D, C is at the left end, B is immediately right of A, and E is left of D.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A three-member committee is selected from P, Q, R and S. If P is selected, Q must also be selected. If Q is selected, R cannot be selected. Which committee is valid?
solution: P,Q,S satisfies P→Q and avoids Q with R. The other choices violate at least one condition.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A meeting must include exactly three of four topics A, B, C and D. A cannot be together with C. B must be included if D is included. Which set is possible?
solution: A,B,D satisfies the A-C restriction and includes B whenever D is present.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: What is the value of x? Statement I: x is an even integer greater than 4 and less than 8. Statement II: x is divisible by 3.
solution: Statement I gives x as 6 or another? The even integers strictly between 4 and 8 are only 6, so I alone is actually sufficient.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Three statements are made: A says, 'B is lying.' B says, 'C is lying.' C says, 'A and B are both lying.' If exactly one person is telling the truth, who is truthful?
solution: If B is truthful, C is lying and A is also lying, giving exactly one truthful speaker.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A candidate is eligible if the candidate has either a degree and two years of experience, or a diploma and five years of experience. Which candidate is eligible?
solution: The third candidate satisfies the first eligibility route exactly.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statements: All policy analysts are researchers. Some researchers are economists. No economist is an auditor. Conclusions: I. Some researchers are not auditors. II. Some policy analysts are not auditors.
solution: The researchers who are economists are not auditors, so I follows. There is no stated existence of policy analysts among those researchers.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: All effective projects have measurable objectives. Some government projects are effective. No project with unclear objectives is measurable. Which conclusion must be true?
options: Some government projects have measurable objectives
No government project has unclear objectives
solution: The effective government projects have measurable objectives by the first statement.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statements: Some managers are trainers. All trainers are communicators. No communicator is isolated from teams. Conclusions: I. Some managers are communicators. II. Some managers are not isolated from teams.
solution: Managers who are trainers are communicators, and communicators are not isolated from teams. Both conclusions follow.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Every audited account is reviewed. Some reviewed accounts are corrected. No corrected account is pending approval. Which conclusion is necessarily true?
options: Some reviewed accounts are not pending approval
No audited account is pending approval
solution: The accounts that are corrected are reviewed and, by the third statement, are not pending approval.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: A pilot program in three districts reduced average document-processing time by 18%, while staffing levels remained unchanged. Conclusions: I. The pilot may have improved process efficiency. II. The same 18% reduction will necessarily occur everywhere.
solution: The observed result supports a possible efficiency improvement. It cannot guarantee an identical result elsewhere.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: An institution requires applicants to submit documents through a single verified portal rather than by email. Conclusions: I. The institution seeks a more controlled submission process. II. Email can never be secure.
solution: A verified portal indicates a controlled submission objective. The absolute claim about all email security is unsupported.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: The ministry should publish quarterly performance dashboards so citizens can track progress. Assumptions: I. Citizens may use performance information to monitor public work. II. Publishing comparable indicators can make progress easier to assess.
solution: The recommendation relies on both the usefulness of information to citizens and the value of comparable indicators.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Statement: Before expanding the scholarship program nationwide, the authority should evaluate the pilot. Assumptions: I. Pilot results can provide evidence relevant to expansion. II. The pilot and nationwide program must be identical in every respect.
solution: Evaluation assumes pilot evidence can inform the decision. Identical conditions everywhere are not necessary.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Assertion (A): An organization should separate approval and payment authorization for major purchases. Reason (R): Separating key controls can reduce the risk that one person can complete an improper transaction without detection.
options: Both are true and R explains A
Both are true but R does not explain A
solution: The reason directly explains the internal-control benefit of separation of duties.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A public transport operator changed routes without consulting traffic data. Afterward, congestion increased at several intersections. Which explanation is most logically plausible?
options: The route change may have shifted traffic into already constrained intersections
Traffic data can never predict congestion
The route change proves every intersection was affected
Congestion is unrelated to transport routes
solution: A route change can redistribute traffic; the other statements are unsupported absolutes.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A hospital introduced an appointment-reminder system and observed fewer missed appointments. Which additional evidence would best strengthen a causal interpretation?
options: Comparison with a similar period or group without the reminder system
The hospital's total number of employees
The color of the reminder messages
solution: A suitable comparison group or period helps distinguish the intervention effect from other changes.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A university reports that students attending a study-support program have higher pass rates. Which factor is most important before claiming the program caused the difference?
options: Whether participants already differed in motivation or prior performance
Whether the program had a logo
Whether the classrooms were painted recently
Whether the report used a short title
solution: Pre-existing differences between participants and non-participants can confound the observed relationship.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: An agency's emergency procurement records show repeated missing justifications. Which course is most appropriate first?
options: Review the cases, identify the control failure, and require documented justification
Ignore the issue because emergencies are unpredictable
solution: A targeted review can identify the weakness and lead to corrective controls without abandoning necessary emergency procurement.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A district must choose one of four projects. Project A has high impact but exceeds the budget. B has moderate impact and fits the budget. C has low impact and fits the budget. D has high impact but lacks a feasibility assessment. If budget compliance and feasibility are mandatory, which should be selected?
solution: B satisfies the mandatory constraints and offers moderate impact; A exceeds budget and D lacks required feasibility assessment.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: An online service becomes unavailable for several hours during a deadline period. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Extend the deadline or provide an alternative channel while investigating the outage
Require applicants to keep trying without notice
solution: A fair contingency protects applicants while the technical problem is investigated.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A supervisor must allocate limited training seats. Priority is given to staff whose roles are directly affected by a new system, then to staff who have not received training before. Which applicant should have highest priority?
options: Staff member affected by the new system and never trained
Staff member unaffected and already trained
Staff member unaffected and never trained
Staff member affected but already trained
solution: The first applicant satisfies both the primary and secondary priority criteria.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Five tasks A, B, C, D and E must be scheduled Monday to Friday, one per day. B must be after A. C must be immediately before D. E must be Friday. Which task must be Wednesday?
solution: Since C-D must be consecutive and E is Friday, the pair must be Monday-Tuesday or Wednesday-Thursday. If Monday-Tuesday, A and B must occupy Wednesday-Thursday, so Wednesday could be A. Thus no listed task must be Wednesday.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Four interviews P, Q, R and S are scheduled in four slots. Q is before R. S is immediately after P. R is not last. Which sequence is valid?
solution: Q-P-S-R satisfies Q before R, S immediately after P, and R is last—so it violates R not last. Therefore none? Check options: P-S-Q-R also has R last; P-Q-S-R has R last; S-P-Q-R has S not after P. Hence no sequence is valid.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A four-person panel is selected from A, B, C, D, E and F. A and B cannot serve together. C must serve if D serves. E cannot serve if F serves. Which panel is valid?
solution: B,C,D,E satisfies A-B restriction; D is accompanied by C; E is not paired with F.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A project team needs exactly three skills: legal, financial and technical. Candidate pairs are: A has legal+financial; B has financial+technical; C has legal+technical; D has legal only. Which pair of candidates covers all three skills?
solution: A supplies legal and financial, while B supplies financial and technical; together all three skills are covered.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: In a ranking, R is above S but below T. U is below S but above V. Which order is necessarily correct from highest to lowest among these five?
solution: T > R > S and S > U > V, so T, R, S, U, V is forced.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Six books P, Q, R, S, T and U are arranged left to right. P is left of Q. R is immediately right of S. T is between Q and U. Which arrangement is possible?
options: P Q T U S R
Q P T U S R
P T Q U S R
P Q U T S R
solution: P-Q-T-U-S-R satisfies P before Q, R immediately after S, and T between Q and U.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A box is labeled either Red or Blue. Exactly one of the following statements is true: (1) The box is Red. (2) The box is not Red. What can be concluded?
options: Exactly one statement is true in either case, so the information does not distinguish the color
solution: For either Red or Blue, exactly one of 'Red' and 'not Red' is true. Thus the condition does not identify the color.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: If a proposal is approved, it receives funding. If a proposal receives funding, monitoring is required. Proposal X has not been monitored. What follows logically?
solution: Approval would imply funding and funding would imply monitoring. Since monitoring did not occur, X could not have been approved under these rules.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Three people A, B and C each either always tell the truth or always lie. A says, 'B is truthful.' B says, 'C is truthful.' C says, 'A and B are different types.' If A is a liar, what must be true?
options: B is truthful and C is truthful
B is a liar and C is truthful
B is truthful and C is a liar
B and C are both liars
solution: A lying means B is not truthful, so B is a liar. B then lies when saying C is truthful, so C is a liar? Wait, if B lies, C is not truthful, hence C is a liar. Therefore D, not B.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A person may enter a restricted room only if they have an access card and are on the approved list. Maya has an access card but is not on the approved list. What follows?
options: Maya must be on the approved list
The rule does not apply to Maya
solution: Both conditions are required; lacking the approved-list condition means Maya may not enter.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Is integer n positive? Statement I: n² = 9. Statement II: n is not equal to -3.
solution: I gives n = 3 or -3. II excludes -3, so together n=3 and is positive.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Is employee P older than employee Q? Statement I: P is older than R. Statement II: R is older than Q.
solution: Together, P > R > Q, so P is older than Q.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: Four departments W, X, Y and Z each receive a different number of complaints. W has more than X. Y has fewer than Z but more than X. Which department must have neither the highest nor the lowest number?
solution: X is below W and Y, while Y is below Z and above X. Thus Y is strictly between X and Z, so it cannot be highest or lowest.

category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
question: A grant is approved only when all three conditions are met: the project is feasible, the budget is within the ceiling, and the required documents are complete. Project P is feasible and within budget, but one required document is missing. What is the correct decision?
options: Approve P because two conditions are met
Do not approve yet; obtain the missing document first
Approve P and waive the document condition
solution: All three conditions are mandatory, so approval should wait until the missing document is supplied.
